<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<article class="ltx_document">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Dayang Liang
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span>Department of Automation, Xiamen University, Xiamen, China
</span></span></span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Ruihan Liu
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span>Department of Computer Science, Beijing Normal-Hong Kong Baptist University, Zhuhai, China

</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">

</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">

</span></span></span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Bo An
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span>College of Computing and Data Science, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore
</span></span></span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Accelerating exploration in visual reinforcement learning under sparse rewards remains challenging due to the substantial task-irrelevant variations. Despite advances in intrinsic exploration, many methods either assume access to low-dimensional states or lack task-aware exploration strategies, thereby rendering them fragile in visual domains. To bridge this gap, we present <span id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">TEB</span>, a <span id="abstract1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">T</span>ask-aware <span id="abstract1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">E</span>xploration approach that tightly couples task-relevant representations with exploration through a predictive <span id="abstract1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">B</span>isimulation metric. Specifically, TEB leverages the metric not only to learn behaviorally grounded task representations but also to measure behaviorally intrinsic novelty over the learned latent space. To realize this, we first theoretically mitigate the representation collapse of degenerate bisimulation metrics under sparse rewards by internally introducing a simple but effective predicted reward differential. Building on this robust metric, we design potential-based exploration bonuses, which measure the relative novelty of adjacent observations over the latent space. Extensive experiments on MetaWorld and Maze2D show that TEB achieves superior exploration ability and outperforms recent baselines.</p>
  
</div>
<div class="ltx_keywords">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_keywords">Keywords: </h6>Machine Learning, ICML
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Visual reinforcement learning (RL) has made significant progress in continuous control <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mu et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, highlighting the potential to learn decision policies directly from high-dimensional visual observations. However, in complex domains, particularly those with sparse or delayed rewards, it remains challenging to improve extrinsic-reward exploration and sample efficiency. To address this, prior work has developed intrinsic-motivation signals based on novelty or uncertainty, including forward prediction-error curiosity <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Pathak et al., 2017</a>)</cite>, Bayesian Surprise <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mazzaglia et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, random network distillation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Burda et al., 2018</a>)</cite>, and ensemble disagreement, as well as density-based objectives such as kNN entropy estimation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mutti et al., 2021</a>)</cite> and state-marginal matching <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee et al., 2019</a>)</cite>. Nonetheless, these intrinsic rewards are often defined over representation spaces that are not rigorously aligned with task semantics <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Pathak et al., 2017</a>; <a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yarats et al., 2021b</a>)</cite>. They are therefore susceptible to nuisance variations such as texture, illumination, and background noise, which can steer behavior away from the core task <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bu et al., 2024</a>)</cite>. In addition, unsupervised skill discovery methods <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bai et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al., 2025</a>)</cite> expand coverage by maximizing skill discriminability or temporal reachability. Although they can provide coverage benefits in theory, they typically rely on accessible ground-truth states and incur substantial overheads, which limits their efficiency and scalability in practical visual environments.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S1.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18724v1/figures/abs_fig.png" id="S1.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/289;" width="476" height="289" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S1.F1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 1</span>: </span><span id="S1.F1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">An illustration of existing explorations in noise space and our task-aware exploration. In complex tasks, existing explorations remain limited by task-irrelevant elements, resulting in risky transitions like the “yellow line”. In contrast, the task-relevant space and exploration bonus built on the bisimulation metric can help visual RL complete tasks faster. The right figure specifically illustrates how to construct an exploration bonus that measures task-relevant novelty between a state relative to a global anchor state using the unified metric in a rigorous task space.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This motivates a central question: <span id="S1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">can we develop a simple mechanism that both captures task structure and quantifies task-relevant exploration bonuses?</span> Bisimulation metrics provide a principled foundation for this goal. By combining differences in rewards and dynamic transitions, bisimulation and its variants measure behavioral equivalence between states <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ferns et al., 2004</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ferns et al., 2011</a>)</cite>, which have previously been used to learn mappings from high-dimensional observations to task-relevant latent spaces <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zang et al., 2024</a>)</cite>. In fact, the metric itself offers a task-aware notion of distance <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, making it a natural candidate for constructing exploration bonuses. Moreover, existing theory shows that the state value difference is bounded by the bisimulation distance <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen and Pan, 2022</a>)</cite>, which suggests that larger bisimulation distances may correspond to larger disparities in long-term returns. These insights motivate a unified perspective in which the same bisimulation metric can underpin both representation learning and intrinsic-reward construction. Nevertheless, the core advantage of bisimulation metrics is vulnerable to sparse or delayed rewards, i.e., sparse rewards can easily lead to metric degradation and further representation collapse <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen and Pan, 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liao et al., 2023</a>)</cite>. Although prior work has attempted to mitigate this issue, for example by eliminating reward variance in the RAP distance <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen and Pan, 2022</a>)</cite>, these approaches remain unstable.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To address these issues, we propose <span id="S1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">TEB</span>, a task-aware exploration approach built on a predictive bisimulation metric. The core idea is to keep the bisimulation metric non-degenerate and representations learnable under sparse rewards, while leveraging the same measurement principle to shape global task-guided exploration bonuses. We briefly summarize the insights in Figure <a href="#S1.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. Concretely, we first introduce a reward predictor that produces Gaussian reward differentials to replace the extrinsic reward differentials used in conventional bisimulation metrics. This prediction-based reward can theoretically guarantee a positive metric radius between states even in the worst-case transitions, which mitigates representation collapse caused by zero-distance metrics. Building on this robust metric, we further construct task-aware intrinsic exploration bonuses. Specifically, we design a potential function <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ng et al., 1999</a>)</cite> based on the metric and then compute relative novelty via potential differences to an approximately global anchor state. This design effectively encourages exploration toward task-relevant regions while preserving the optimal policy in theory.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">We extensively evaluate TEB on MetaWorld <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yu et al., 2020</a>)</cite> and Maze2D <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Campos et al., 2020</a>)</cite> environments. The results demonstrate that TEB achieves superior policy perfermance in challenging visual tasks and also outperforms powerful intrinsic exploration baselines on low-dimensional Maze2D tasks. Ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of TEB components. Our contributions are threefold.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">(1) We propose a visual RL method that tightly couples task representations and task-aware exploration through a predictive bisimulation metric.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">(2) We introduce a simple yet effective predictive bisimulation formulation that extends the metric-based representation to sparse-reward visual settings.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">(3) We construct a metric-based intrinsic reward that encourages policies to perform task-aware explorations in the representation space.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Preliminaries</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We assume that the underlying environment is a discounted Markov decision process (MDP) defined by the tuple <math id="S2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}=\langle\mathcal{S},\mathcal{A},\mathcal{P},r,\gamma\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}=\langle\mathcal{S},\mathcal{A},\mathcal{P},r,\gamma\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>,
where <math id="S2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the state space, <math id="S2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math> the action space,
<math id="S2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}(s^{\prime}|s,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}(s^{\prime}|s,a)</annotation></semantics></math> the state transition function that captures the probability from <math id="S2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> given action <math id="S2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r(s,a)\in\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(s,a)\in\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math> the reward function, and <math id="S2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma\in[0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma\in[0,1)</annotation></semantics></math> the discount factor. A
policy <math id="S2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(a|s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(a|s)</annotation></semantics></math> presents the probability when select <math id="S2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> conditioned on a state <math id="S2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>. The value function <math id="S2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V^{\pi}:\mathcal{S}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>V</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V^{\pi}:\mathcal{S}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math> is defined as the expected cumulative discounted rewards,</p>
<table id="S2.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V^{\pi}(s)=\mathbb{E}_{\begin{subarray}{c}a_{t}\sim\pi\\
s_{t+1}\sim{\mathcal{P}}\end{subarray}}\Big[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}r(s_{t},a_{t})|s_{0}=s\Big]" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>V</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mtable rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>∼</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">[</mo><mrow><mrow><munderover><mo lspace="0em" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></munderover><mrow><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>t</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V^{\pi}(s)=\mathbb{E}_{\begin{subarray}{c}a_{t}\sim\pi\\
s_{t+1}\sim{\mathcal{P}}\end{subarray}}\Big[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}r(s_{t},a_{t})|s_{0}=s\Big]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The RL goal is to learn an optimal policy <math id="S2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi^{*}=\text{argmax}_{\pi}V^{\pi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>π</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mtext>argmax</mtext><mi>π</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>V</mi><mi>π</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi^{*}=\text{argmax}_{\pi}V^{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math> that maximizes cumulative discounted rewards. In high-dimensional vision tasks, we also jointly learn an encoder <math id="S2.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{\omega}:\mathcal{S}\rightarrow\mathcal{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>ω</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒵</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{\omega}:\mathcal{S}\rightarrow\mathcal{Z}</annotation></semantics></math> that maps high-dimensional observations <math id="S2.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s\in\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s\in\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math> to a low-dimensional latent space <math id="S2.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z\in\mathcal{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒵</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z\in\mathcal{Z}</annotation></semantics></math>, while retaining only task-relevant information for learning a parameterized policy <math id="S2.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(a|\phi_{\omega}(s))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>ω</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(a|\phi_{\omega}(s))</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.1 </span>Bisimulation Metrics</h3>

<div id="S2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The bisimulation metric <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ferns et al., 2004</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ferns et al., 2011</a>)</cite> measures behavioral similarity between states by defining a pseudometric <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d:\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{S}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d:\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{S}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}</annotation></semantics></math> over a reward differential term and a 1-Wasserstein distance in dynamics models. Theorem <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 2.1 (𝜋-bisimulation metric ( , ) ). ‣ 2.1 Bisimulation Metrics ‣ 2 Preliminaries ‣ Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a> is a policy-dependent bisimulation metric, which focuses on behaviors relative to a specific policy.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S2.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 2.1</span></span><span id="S2.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(<math id="S2.Thmtheorem1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>-bisimulation metric <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Castro, 2020</a>)</cite> )<span id="S2.Thmtheorem1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.Thmtheorem1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.Thmtheorem1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Given a MDP <math id="S2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math> and a fixed policy <math id="S2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, the following on-policy bisimulation metric exists and is unique:</span></p>

</table>
<p id="S2.Thmtheorem1.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.Thmtheorem1.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where the <math id="S2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{\pi}_{s}=\mathbb{E}_{a\sim\pi}[r(s,a)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{\pi}_{s}=\mathbb{E}_{a\sim\pi}[r(s,a)]</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathcal{P}_{s_{i}}^{\pi}=\mathbb{E}_{a\sim\pi}\mathcal{P}^{\pi}(\cdot|s_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}_{s_{i}}^{\pi}=\mathbb{E}_{a\sim\pi}\mathcal{P}^{\pi}(\cdot|s_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{W}_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{R}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{T}\in[0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{T}\in[0,1)</annotation></semantics></math> are the coefficients of the reward and transition terms of the metric, respectively. <math id="S2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d^{\pi}\left(s_{i},s_{j}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d^{\pi}\left(s_{i},s_{j}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> has a least fixed point <math id="S2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{B}^{\pi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{B}^{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{B}^{\pi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{B}^{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math> is a <math id="S2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>-bisimulation metric.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The central idea behind bisimulation metric-based representation learning is to embed task-relevant features that are associated with the abstract semantics of both rewards and transition dynamics, from high-dimensional observations into a compact latent space <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2021</a>)</cite>. This is typically achieved by minimizing the discrepancy between the latent distance <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\phi_{\omega}(s_{i})-\phi_{\omega}(s_{j})\|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>ω</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>ω</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\phi_{\omega}(s_{i})-\phi_{\omega}(s_{j})\|</annotation></semantics></math> and the bisimulation distance <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d^{\pi}(s_{i},s_{j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d^{\pi}(s_{i},s_{j})</annotation></semantics></math> for any state pairs <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="S2.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{\text{bisim}}=\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\|\phi_{\omega}(s_{i})-\phi_{\omega}(s_{j})\|-d^{\pi}(s_{i},s_{j})\right)^{2}\right]" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><mtext>bisim</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>ω</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>ω</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{\text{bisim}}=\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\|\phi_{\omega}(s_{i})-\phi_{\omega}(s_{j})\|-d^{\pi}(s_{i},s_{j})\right)^{2}\right]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Method</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we present task-aware exploration with a predictive bisimulation metric (TEB) in detail. The proposed method aims to tightly couple visual representation learning with intrinsic exploration by constructing a robust bisimulation metric. We begin by analyzing the limitations of conventional bisimulation metric-based representation learning under sparse rewards. We then introduce a predictive bisimulation metric that remains non-degenerate under sparse rewards and provide theoretical guarantees. Finally, we design a potential-based exploration bonus derived from this metric over the learned task-relevant space and prove its invariance with respect to the optimal policy.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>The Risk of Bisimulation Metrics</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Bisimulation metrics for learning a grounded task-relevant representation space hold great promise. To make them scalable, prior work introduces the policy-dependent bisimulation metric <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d^{\pi}(s_{i},s_{j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d^{\pi}(s_{i},s_{j})</annotation></semantics></math>, which estimates behavioral similarity from transition samples collected under a fixed policy <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Castro, 2020</a>)</cite>, making it practical and tractable. Despite this appeal, the metric remains challenging to scale in sparse reward settings. Intuitively, when <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|r^{\pi}_{s_{i}}-r^{\pi}_{s_{j}}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mi>π</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|r^{\pi}_{s_{i}}-r^{\pi}_{s_{j}}|</annotation></semantics></math> is frequently near zero, the fixed-point recursion in Eq. (<a href="#S2.E2" title="Equation 2 ‣ Theorem 2.1 (𝜋-bisimulation metric ( , ) ). ‣ 2.1 Bisimulation Metrics ‣ 2 Preliminaries ‣ Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>) aggressively contracts distances as the reward term provides negligible scale, and the Wasserstein term is discounted by <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{T}&lt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{T}&lt;1</annotation></semantics></math>. Theoretically, existing analysis shows that the metric diameter is upper bounded by reward differentials.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 3.1</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Diameter of <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math> is bounded <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kemertas and Aumentado-Armstrong, 2021</a>)</cite>)<span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">On-policy <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>-bisimulation metric <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{d}^{\pi}:\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{S}\rightarrow[0,\infty)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{d}^{\pi}:\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{S}\rightarrow[0,\infty)</annotation></semantics></math> has a fixed upper bound on the diameter of <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
<table id="S3.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{diam}(\mathcal{S};d^{\pi})\leq\frac{c_{R}}{1-c_{T}}\max_{s_{i},s_{j}}\lvert r^{\pi}_{s_{i}}-r^{\pi}_{s_{j}}\rvert." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>diam</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>d</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mfrac><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mi>π</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{diam}(\mathcal{S};d^{\pi})\leq\frac{c_{R}}{1-c_{T}}\max_{s_{i},s_{j}}\lvert r^{\pi}_{s_{i}}-r^{\pi}_{s_{j}}\rvert.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Lemma <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem1" title="Lemma 3.1 (Diameter of 𝒮 is bounded ( , )). ‣ 3.1 The Risk of Bisimulation Metrics ‣ 3 Method ‣ Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a> suggests that the bisimulation metric is theoretically dependent on the inner reward differential term.
If the immediate reward signal remains within a negligible range over a long period, for instance, <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{\pi}_{s}\equiv 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mo>≡</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{\pi}_{s}\equiv 0</annotation></semantics></math>, then the bisimulation metric degenerates to the trivial solution <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{S},d^{\pi})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>diam</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>d</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{S},d^{\pi})=0</annotation></semantics></math>, which in turn induces an erroneous collapse of task-relevant distances in the learned latent representation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>The Proposed Predictive Bisimulation Metric</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Predictive Bisimulation Metric.</span> To prevent representation collapse caused by zero-distance metric under sparse reward settings, we propose the robust predictive bisimulation metric by replacing the reward differential with a predictive reward differential <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta^{\pi}_{R}(s_{i},s_{j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta^{\pi}_{R}(s_{i},s_{j})</annotation></semantics></math>. Our predictive bisimulation metric operator on ground-truth states is defined by</p>

<p id="S3.SS2.p1.4" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{R}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{R}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{T}\in[0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{T}\in[0,1)</annotation></semantics></math>. <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{r}_{\theta}(s,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{r}_{\theta}(s,a)</annotation></semantics></math> denotes a random variable sampled from the predicted reward distribution <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="p_{\theta}(\cdot|s,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\theta}(\cdot|s,a)</annotation></semantics></math> with parameters <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> under the action induced by a specific policy. <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{\mathcal{P}}^{\pi}=\mathbb{E}_{a\sim\pi}\mathcal{\widehat{P}}(s_{i},a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>π</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{\mathcal{P}}^{\pi}=\mathbb{E}_{a\sim\pi}\mathcal{\widehat{P}}(s_{i},a)</annotation></semantics></math> is a learned policy-marginal transition model. When <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{r}_{\theta}(s,a)=r(s,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{r}_{\theta}(s,a)=r(s,a)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{\mathcal{P}}^{\pi}={\mathcal{P}}^{\pi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>π</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>π</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{\mathcal{P}}^{\pi}={\mathcal{P}}^{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math>, Eq. (<a href="#S3.E5" title="Equation 5 ‣ 3.2 The Proposed Predictive Bisimulation Metric ‣ 3 Method ‣ Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>) reduces to the standard on-policy bisimulation metric.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 3.2</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Convergence and Fixed Point)<span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Predictive bisimulation metric <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{d}_{\text{pre}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">pre</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{d}_{\text{pre}}</annotation></semantics></math> is a contraction mapping w.r.t the <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>L</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math> norm on <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{S}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{S}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and there exists a fixed-point <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{d}_{\text{pre}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">pre</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{d}_{\text{pre}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The proof of Lemma <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem2" title="Lemma 3.2 (Convergence and Fixed Point). ‣ 3.2 The Proposed Predictive Bisimulation Metric ‣ 3 Method ‣ Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a> is available in Appendix <a href="#A1.SS1" title="A.1 The Proof of the Convergence and Fixed Point ‣ Appendix A Theoretical Analysis ‣ Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.1</span></a>. This provides a theoretical convergence property for bootstrapped metric and representation learning based on the predictive bisimulation metric.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Gaussian Reward Predictor.</span>  We assume that the external reward is Gaussian distributed. Then, let <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="p_{\theta}(\cdot|s_{t},a_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\theta}(\cdot|s_{t},a_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> be a Gaussian predictor, which outputs a distribution probabilistic conditioned on the current state and action. We model it on the latent space <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒵</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{Z}</annotation></semantics></math> by,</p>
<table id="S3.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\theta}(r_{t}|s_{t},a_{t};\omega)=\mathcal{N}\!\big(\mu_{\theta}(z_{t},a_{t}),\sigma^{2}_{\theta}(z_{t},a_{t})\big)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>;</mo><mi>ω</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.798em;" width="0.798em"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\theta}(r_{t}|s_{t},a_{t};\omega)=\mathcal{N}\!\big(\mu_{\theta}(z_{t},a_{t}),\sigma^{2}_{\theta}(z_{t},a_{t})\big)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p3.2" class="ltx_p">where the mean <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> and the variance <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> are learned networks, as well as the latent state <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}=\phi_{\omega}(s_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>ω</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}=\phi_{\omega}(s_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>. We train the reward predictor by minimizing the negative log-likelihood on replay data,</p>
<table id="S3.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.E8"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
