<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Theoretical Analysis</h2>

<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>The Proof of the Convergence and Fixed Point</h3>

<div id="A1.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A1.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma A.1</span></span><span id="A1.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Convergence and Fixed Point)<span id="A1.Thmtheorem1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Predictive bisimulation metric <math id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{d}_{\text{pre}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">pre</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{d}_{\text{pre}}</annotation></semantics></math> is a contraction mapping w.r.t the <math id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>L</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math> norm on <math id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{S}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{S}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and there exists a fixed-point <math id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{d}_{\text{pre}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">pre</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{d}_{\text{pre}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">We refer to the work of Kemertas et al. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kemertas and Aumentado-Armstrong, 2021</a>)</cite> to prove this. Take any <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d,d^{\prime}\in\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d,d^{\prime}\in\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math> and any state pair <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(s_{i},s_{j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(s_{i},s_{j})</annotation></semantics></math>.
By the operator definition in Eq. (<a href="#S3.E5" title="Equation 5 ‣ 3.2 The Proposed Predictive Bisimulation Metric ‣ 3 Method ‣ Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>),
the predictive reward differential <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{R}^{\pi}(s_{i},s_{j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{R}^{\pi}(s_{i},s_{j})</annotation></semantics></math> does not depend on <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>,
hence it cancels:</span></p>
<table id="A1.EGx2" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.Ex2"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>

<div id="A1.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mu:=\widehat{\mathcal{P}}^{\pi}(\cdot|s_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>:=</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>π</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu:=\widehat{\mathcal{P}}^{\pi}(\cdot|s_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\nu:=\widehat{\mathcal{P}}^{\pi}(\cdot|s_{j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ν</mi><mo>:=</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>π</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu:=\widehat{\mathcal{P}}^{\pi}(\cdot|s_{j})</annotation></semantics></math>.
Using the primal form of the <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>-Wasserstein distance induced by a ground metric <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>

<p id="A1.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">where <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pi(\mu,\nu)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pi(\mu,\nu)</annotation></semantics></math> is the set of couplings with marginals <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>μ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ν</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then we can bound the difference between the two Wasserstein terms as</span></p>
<table id="A1.EGx4" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<p id="A1.SS1.p2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p2.3.1" class="ltx_text">Combining Eq. (<a href="#A1.E16" title="Equation 16 ‣ Proof. ‣ A.1 The Proof of the Convergence and Fixed Point ‣ Appendix A Theoretical Analysis ‣ Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a>) and Eq. (<a href="#A1.E18" title="Equation 18 ‣ Proof. ‣ A.1 The Proof of the Convergence and Fixed Point ‣ Appendix A Theoretical Analysis ‣ Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a>) yields</span></p>

</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.p2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p2.4.1" class="ltx_text">Taking the supremum over <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(s_{i},s_{j})\in\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(s_{i},s_{j})\in\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math> gives</span></p>
<table id="A1.EGx6" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\|\widehat{\mathcal{T}}^{\pi}d-\widehat{\mathcal{T}}^{\pi}d^{\prime}\|_{\infty}\leq c_{T}\|d-d^{\prime}\|_{\infty}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>π</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>π</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\|\widehat{\mathcal{T}}^{\pi}d-\widehat{\mathcal{T}}^{\pi}d^{\prime}\|_{\infty}\leq c_{T}\|d-d^{\prime}\|_{\infty}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(20)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.p2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p2.5.1" class="ltx_text">Since <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{T}\in[0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{T}\in[0,1)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{\mathcal{T}}^{\pi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>π</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{\mathcal{T}}^{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math> is a contraction on <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m11" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="(\mathcal{M},\|\cdot\|_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∥</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mathcal{M},\|\cdot\|_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math>.
By the Banach fixed-point theorem, there exists a unique fixed point
<math id="A1.SS1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{d}_{\text{pre}}\in\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mtext>pre</mtext></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{d}_{\text{pre}}\in\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math> such that
<math id="A1.SS1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{d}_{\text{pre}}=\widehat{\mathcal{T}}^{\pi}\widetilde{d}_{\text{pre}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mtext>pre</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>π</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mtext>pre</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{d}_{\text{pre}}=\widehat{\mathcal{T}}^{\pi}\widetilde{d}_{\text{pre}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>The Proof of the Predictive Reward Prevents Degenerate Metric</h3>

<div id="A1.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A1.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem A.2</span></span><span id="A1.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Predictive Reward Prevents Degenerate Metric)<span id="A1.Thmtheorem2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A1.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let the state space <math id="A1.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math> be compact and the policy <math id="A1.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> fixed.
Consider the predictive bisimulation operator <math id="A1.Thmtheorem2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{\mathcal{T}}^{\pi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>π</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{\mathcal{T}}^{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math>, the learned reward model satisfies
<math id="A1.Thmtheorem2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{r}_{\theta}(s_{t},a_{t})=r_{t}+\varepsilon_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{r}_{\theta}(s_{t},a_{t})=r_{t}+\varepsilon_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A1.Thmtheorem2.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathrm{Var}[\varepsilon_{t}|s_{t},a_{t}]=\Sigma&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Var</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Var}[\varepsilon_{t}|s_{t},a_{t}]=\Sigma&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then, the unique fixed point <math id="A1.Thmtheorem2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{d}_{\text{pre}}=\widehat{\mathcal{T}}^{\pi}\widetilde{d}_{\text{pre}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">pre</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>π</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">pre</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{d}_{\text{pre}}=\widehat{\mathcal{T}}^{\pi}\widetilde{d}_{\text{pre}}</annotation></semantics></math>
admits a strictly positive expected diameter in the sparse-reward region
<math id="A1.Thmtheorem2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}_{0}=\{s|r(s,a)=0\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}_{0}=\{s|r(s,a)=0\}</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></p>
<table id="A1.E21" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<div id="A1.SS2.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">Fix <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> and consider <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(s_{i},s_{j})\in\mathcal{S}_{0}\times\mathcal{S}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(s_{i},s_{j})\in\mathcal{S}_{0}\times\mathcal{S}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> sampled from <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}</annotation></semantics></math>.
By the fixed-point equation of <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{d}_{\mathrm{pre}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>pre</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{d}_{\mathrm{pre}}</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>

</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text">where <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{R}^{\pi}(s_{i},s_{j})=\mathbb{E}_{a_{i},a_{j}\sim\pi}\big[\big|\hat{r}_{\theta}(s_{i},a_{i})-\hat{r}_{\theta}(s_{j},a_{j})\big|\big]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{R}^{\pi}(s_{i},s_{j})=\mathbb{E}_{a_{i},a_{j}\sim\pi}\big[\big|\hat{r}_{\theta}(s_{i},a_{i})-\hat{r}_{\theta}(s_{j},a_{j})\big|\big]</annotation></semantics></math>.
Since <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{W}_{1}(\cdot)\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{W}_{1}(\cdot)\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{R}^{\pi}\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{R}^{\pi}\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math>, we immediately have</span></p>

<div id="A1.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">For the upper bound, take <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{D}}[\cdot]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{D}}[\cdot]</annotation></semantics></math> on both sides of (<a href="#A1.E22" title="Equation 22 ‣ Proof. ‣ A.2 The Proof of the Predictive Reward Prevents Degenerate Metric ‣ Appendix A Theoretical Analysis ‣ Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">22</span></a>).
Using the primal form of <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and choosing the product coupling gives
<math id="A1.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{1}(\tilde{d}_{\mathrm{pre}})(\mu,\nu)\leq\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\mu,y\sim\nu}[\tilde{d}_{\mathrm{pre}}(x,y)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>pre</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>μ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>ν</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>pre</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{1}(\tilde{d}_{\mathrm{pre}})(\mu,\nu)\leq\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\mu,y\sim\nu}[\tilde{d}_{\mathrm{pre}}(x,y)]</annotation></semantics></math>. The expected cost under this product coupling is bounded by the same pairwise expectation,
hence</span></p>

<p id="A1.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">Substituting (<a href="#A1.E24" title="Equation 24 ‣ Proof. ‣ A.2 The Proof of the Predictive Reward Prevents Degenerate Metric ‣ Appendix A Theoretical Analysis ‣ Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">24</span></a>) into the expectation of (<a href="#A1.E22" title="Equation 22 ‣ Proof. ‣ A.2 The Proof of the Predictive Reward Prevents Degenerate Metric ‣ Appendix A Theoretical Analysis ‣ Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">22</span></a>) yields</span></p>

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{D}}\big[\tilde{d}_{\mathrm{pre}}(s_{i},s_{j})\big]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>pre</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{D}}\big[\tilde{d}_{\mathrm{pre}}(s_{i},s_{j})\big]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\leq c_{R}\,\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{D}}\big[\Delta_{R}^{\pi}(s_{i},s_{j})\big]+c_{T}\,\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{D}}\big[\tilde{d}_{\mathrm{pre}}(s_{i},s_{j})\big]," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>pre</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\leq c_{R}\,\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{D}}\big[\Delta_{R}^{\pi}(s_{i},s_{j})\big]+c_{T}\,\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{D}}\big[\tilde{d}_{\mathrm{pre}}(s_{i},s_{j})\big],</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E25.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\leq\frac{c_{R}}{1-c_{T}}\,\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{D}}\big[\Delta_{R}^{\pi}(s_{i},s_{j})\big]." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\leq\frac{c_{R}}{1-c_{T}}\,\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{D}}\big[\Delta_{R}^{\pi}(s_{i},s_{j})\big].</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="A1.SS2.p2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p2.3.1" class="ltx_text">It remains to bound <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{D}}\!\left[\Delta_{R}^{\pi}\right]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{D}}\!\left[\Delta_{R}^{\pi}\right]</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>.
For <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s\in\mathcal{S}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s\in\mathcal{S}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> we have <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r(s,a)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(s,a)=0</annotation></semantics></math>, so the learned reward model satisfies
<math id="A1.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{r}_{\theta}(s,a)=r(s,a)+\varepsilon=\varepsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>ε</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>ε</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{r}_{\theta}(s,a)=r(s,a)+\varepsilon=\varepsilon</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathrm{Var}[\varepsilon\mid s,a]=\Sigma&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Var</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>ε</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Var}[\varepsilon\mid s,a]=\Sigma&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.
Therefore, for <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(s_{i},s_{j})\in\mathcal{S}_{0}\times\mathcal{S}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(s_{i},s_{j})\in\mathcal{S}_{0}\times\mathcal{S}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="A1.SS2.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{r}_{\theta}(s_{i},a_{i})-\hat{r}_{\theta}(s_{j},a_{j})=\varepsilon_{i}-\varepsilon_{j}~\triangleq~\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.608em">≜</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{r}_{\theta}(s_{i},a_{i})-\hat{r}_{\theta}(s_{j},a_{j})=\varepsilon_{i}-\varepsilon_{j}~\triangleq~\delta</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta</annotation></semantics></math> is a non-degenerate Gaussian.
If <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> are conditionally independent given <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(s_{i},a_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(s_{i},a_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(s_{j},a_{j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(s_{j},a_{j})</annotation></semantics></math>, then
<math id="A1.SS2.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Var}[\delta]=2\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Var</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Var}[\delta]=2\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, and hence <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta\sim\mathcal{N}(0,2\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta\sim\mathcal{N}(0,2\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Let <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta=\sqrt{2\Sigma}\,z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta=\sqrt{2\Sigma}\,z</annotation></semantics></math> and</span></p>

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\sqrt{2\Sigma}\,\mathbb{E}\big[|z|\big]=\sqrt{2\Sigma}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{\pi}}\sqrt{\Sigma}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msqrt><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mfrac></mstyle></msqrt></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mi>π</mi></msqrt></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi></msqrt></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\sqrt{2\Sigma}\,\mathbb{E}\big[|z|\big]=\sqrt{2\Sigma}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{\pi}}\sqrt{\Sigma}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="A1.SS2.p2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p2.4.1" class="ltx_text">Moreover, <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[|\delta|]&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[|\delta|]&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> since <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.
Therefore, on <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> we have</span></p>

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{D}}\mathbb{E}_{a_{i},a_{j}\sim\pi}\Big[\big|\hat{r}_{\theta}(s_{i},a_{i})-\hat{r}_{\theta}(s_{j},a_{j})\big|\Big]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">[</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{D}}\mathbb{E}_{a_{i},a_{j}\sim\pi}\Big[\big|\hat{r}_{\theta}(s_{i},a_{i})-\hat{r}_{\theta}(s_{j},a_{j})\big|\Big]</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(26)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.p2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p2.5.1" class="ltx_text">Combining this with (35)–(37) gives</span></p>
<table id="A1.EGx13" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.Ex11"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle 0&lt;\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{D}}\!\left[\tilde{d}_{\mathrm{pre}}(s_{i},s_{j})\right]~\leq~\frac{c_{R}}{1-c_{T}}\cdot\frac{2}{\sqrt{\pi}}\sqrt{\Sigma}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>pre</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.330em">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.608em">≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mi>π</mi></msqrt></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi></msqrt></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle 0&lt;\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{D}}\!\left[\tilde{d}_{\mathrm{pre}}(s_{i},s_{j})\right]~\leq~\frac{c_{R}}{1-c_{T}}\cdot\frac{2}{\sqrt{\pi}}\sqrt{\Sigma}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(39)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.p2.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p2.6.1" class="ltx_text">By definition of <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{diam}(\mathcal{S}_{0};\tilde{d}_{\mathrm{pre}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>diam</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>pre</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{diam}(\mathcal{S}_{0};\tilde{d}_{\mathrm{pre}})</annotation></semantics></math> as the expected pairwise distance over
<math id="A1.SS2.p2.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}_{0}\times\mathcal{S}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}_{0}\times\mathcal{S}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> under <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}</annotation></semantics></math>, we proved it.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.3 </span>The Proof of the Value Difference Bound</h3>

<div id="A1.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A1.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem A.3</span></span><span id="A1.Thmtheorem3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Value Difference Bound)<span id="A1.Thmtheorem3.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A1.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Given states <math id="A1.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>, and a policy <math id="A1.Thmtheorem3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="A1.Thmtheorem3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V^{\pi}(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>V</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V^{\pi}(s)</annotation></semantics></math> be the state value function over policy <math id="A1.Thmtheorem3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, we have,</span></p>
<table id="A1.Ex12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\big|V^{\pi}(s_{i})-V^{\pi}(s_{j})\big|\leq\tilde{d}_{\mathrm{pre}}(s_{i},s_{j})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>V</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi>V</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>pre</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\big|V^{\pi}(s_{i})-V^{\pi}(s_{j})\big|\leq\tilde{d}_{\mathrm{pre}}(s_{i},s_{j}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">We prove the theorem by induction based on the work of Chen et al. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen and Pan, 2022</a>)</cite>. We assume the predictive reward random variable <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{r}_{\theta}(s,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{r}_{\theta}(s,a)</annotation></semantics></math> satisfies
<math id="A1.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\hat{r}_{\theta}(s,a)]=r(s,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\hat{r}_{\theta}(s,a)]=r(s,a)</annotation></semantics></math> (equivalently, <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{r}_{\theta}(s,a)=r(s,a)+\varepsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>ε</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{r}_{\theta}(s,a)=r(s,a)+\varepsilon</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\varepsilon|s,a]=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>ε</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\varepsilon|s,a]=0</annotation></semantics></math>),
and we use the transition <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathcal{P}^{\pi}(\cdot|s)=\mathbb{E}_{a\sim\pi(\cdot|s)}\mathcal{P}(\cdot|s,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}^{\pi}(\cdot|s)=\mathbb{E}_{a\sim\pi(\cdot|s)}\mathcal{P}(\cdot|s,a)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Firstly, we provide the following Bellman and metric iterate forms, as well as a key inequality. We define the standard Bellman evaluation operator with the environment reward <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r(s,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(s,a)</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="A1.EGx14" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E27"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E27.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle(\mathcal{T}^{\pi}V)(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle(\mathcal{T}^{\pi}V)(s)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E27.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle:=~\mathbb{E}_{a\sim\pi(\cdot|s)}\!\big[r(s,a)\big]~+~\gamma~\mathbb{E}_{s^{\prime}\sim\mathcal{P}^{\pi}(\cdot|s)}\!\big[V(s^{\prime})\big]," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo rspace="0em">:</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.608em">=</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mi>r</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" rspace="0.330em">]</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.552em">+</mo><mi>γ</mi><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>∼</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mi>π</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mi>V</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle:=~\mathbb{E}_{a\sim\pi(\cdot|s)}\!\big[r(s,a)\big]~+~\gamma~\mathbb{E}_{s^{\prime}\sim\mathcal{P}^{\pi}(\cdot|s)}\!\big[V(s^{\prime})\big],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(27)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS3.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">with <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{0}^{\pi}(\cdot)\equiv 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mn>0</mn><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≡</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{0}^{\pi}(\cdot)\equiv 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{n+1}^{\pi}=\mathcal{T}^{\pi}V_{n}^{\pi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{n+1}^{\pi}=\mathcal{T}^{\pi}V_{n}^{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">We consider the predictive bisimulation operator defined in Eq. (<a href="#S3.E5" title="Equation 5 ‣ 3.2 The Proposed Predictive Bisimulation Metric ‣ 3 Method ‣ Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>):</span></p>

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E28.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle:=~c_{R}\Delta_{R}^{\pi}(s_{i},s_{j})~+~c_{T}~\mathcal{W}_{1}(d)\!\left(\mathcal{P}^{\pi}(\cdot|s_{i}),\mathcal{P}^{\pi}(\cdot|s_{j})\right)," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo rspace="0em">:</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.608em">=</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.330em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.552em">+</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mpadded style="width:0.219em;" width="0.219em"><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mpadded></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle:=~c_{R}\Delta_{R}^{\pi}(s_{i},s_{j})~+~c_{T}~\mathcal{W}_{1}(d)\!\left(\mathcal{P}^{\pi}(\cdot|s_{i}),\mathcal{P}^{\pi}(\cdot|s_{j})\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(28)</span></td></tr></tbody>

<p id="A1.SS3.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">where</span></p>
<table id="A1.EGx16" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<p id="A1.SS3.p6.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p6.2.1" class="ltx_text">For the first term, using <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\hat{r}_{\theta}(s,a)]=r(s,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\hat{r}_{\theta}(s,a)]=r(s,a)</annotation></semantics></math> and the property of <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\mathbb{E}[X]|\leq\mathbb{E}[|X|]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\mathbb{E}[X]|\leq\mathbb{E}[|X|]</annotation></semantics></math>, we have,</span></p>

<p id="A1.SS3.p6.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p6.3.1" class="ltx_text">For the second term, the induction hypothesis implies <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|V_{n}^{\pi}(x)-V_{n}^{\pi}(y)|\leq d_{n}(x,y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|V_{n}^{\pi}(x)-V_{n}^{\pi}(y)|\leq d_{n}(x,y)</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x,y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x,y</annotation></semantics></math>, hence applying
(<a href="#A1.E31" title="Equation 31 ‣ Proof. ‣ A.3 The Proof of the Value Difference Bound ‣ Appendix A Theoretical Analysis ‣ Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">31</span></a>) with <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f=V_{n}^{\pi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f=V_{n}^{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=d_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=d_{n}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m8" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mu=\mathcal{P}^{\pi}(\cdot|s_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu=\mathcal{P}^{\pi}(\cdot|s_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m9" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\nu=\mathcal{P}^{\pi}(\cdot|s_{j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ν</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>π</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu=\mathcal{P}^{\pi}(\cdot|s_{j})</annotation></semantics></math> gives that,</span></p>

<section id="A1.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.4 </span>The Proof the Policy Invariance of Predicted Bisimulation Shaping</h3>

<div id="A1.Thmtheorem4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A1.Thmtheorem4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem A.4</span></span><span id="A1.Thmtheorem4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Policy Invariance of Metric-based Shaping)<span id="A1.Thmtheorem4.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A1.Thmtheorem4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.Thmtheorem4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.Thmtheorem4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="A1.Thmtheorem4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}=(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{A},\mathcal{P},r,\gamma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}=(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{A},\mathcal{P},r,\gamma)</annotation></semantics></math> denote the original MDP, and consider the modified reward function <math id="A1.Thmtheorem4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{\prime}=r+\eta\,F(s,a,a^{\prime})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>F</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{\prime}=r+\eta\,F(s,a,a^{\prime})</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A1.Thmtheorem4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>F</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F</annotation></semantics></math> is defined in Eq (<a href="#S3.E14" title="Equation 14 ‣ 3.3 Metric-based Intrinsic Exploration ‣ 3 Method ‣ Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a>). Then the modified MDP <math id="A1.Thmtheorem4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}^{\prime}=(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{A},\mathcal{P},r^{\prime},\gamma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}^{\prime}=(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{A},\mathcal{P},r^{\prime},\gamma)</annotation></semantics></math> with the metric-based potential preserves the optimal policy of <math id="A1.Thmtheorem4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math> by,</span></p>
<table id="A1.E39" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E39.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{\mathcal{M}^{\prime}}^{*}(s,a)=Q_{\mathcal{M}}^{*}(s,a)-\eta\,\Phi(s),\quad\forall s\in\mathcal{S}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∀</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{\mathcal{M}^{\prime}}^{*}(s,a)=Q_{\mathcal{M}}^{*}(s,a)-\eta\,\Phi(s),\quad\forall s\in\mathcal{S}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(39)</span></td></tr></tbody>

</div>

<div id="A1.SS4.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A1.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">Given the potential shaping <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F(s_{t},a,s^{\prime})=\gamma\,\Phi(s^{\prime})-\Phi(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(s_{t},a,s^{\prime})=\gamma\,\Phi(s^{\prime})-\Phi(s)</annotation></semantics></math> and modified reward <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{\prime}(s,a,s^{\prime})=r(s,a,s^{\prime})+\eta F(s,a,s^{\prime})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>F</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{\prime}(s,a,s^{\prime})=r(s,a,s^{\prime})+\eta F(s,a,s^{\prime})</annotation></semantics></math>. According to the Bellman optimality equation, the optimal action-value function of the original MDP <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math> has the form,</span></p>
