encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\gamma\max_{a^{\prime}}\Big(\big(Q^{\ast}_{\mathcal{M}}(s^{\prime},a^{\prime})-\eta\Phi(s^{\prime})\big)+\eta\Phi(s^{\prime})\Big)=\gamma\eta\Phi(s^{\prime})+\gamma\max_{a^{\prime}}\big(Q^{\ast}_{\mathcal{M}}(s^{\prime},a^{\prime})-\eta\Phi(s^{\prime})\big).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(42)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Then, combining Eq. (<a href="#A1.E41" title="Equation 41 ‣ Proof. ‣ A.4 The Proof the Policy Invariance of Predicted Bisimulation Shaping ‣ Appendix A Theoretical Analysis ‣ Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">41</span></a>) with <math id="A1.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{Q}(s,a)\triangleq Q^{\ast}_{\mathcal{M}}(s,a)-\eta\Phi(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Q}(s,a)\triangleq Q^{\ast}_{\mathcal{M}}(s,a)-\eta\Phi(s)</annotation></semantics></math>, we have,</span></p>
<table id="A1.E43" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E43.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\hat{Q}(s,a)=\mathbb{E}_{s^{\prime}\sim\mathcal{P}(\cdot|s,a)}\Big[r^{\prime}(s,a,s^{\prime})+\gamma\max_{a^{\prime}}\hat{Q}(s^{\prime},a^{\prime})\Big]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>∼</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">[</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>γ</mi><munder><mi>max</mi><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></munder><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Q}(s,a)=\mathbb{E}_{s^{\prime}\sim\mathcal{P}(\cdot|s,a)}\Big[r^{\prime}(s,a,s^{\prime})+\gamma\max_{a^{\prime}}\hat{Q}(s^{\prime},a^{\prime})\Big],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(43)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS4.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS4.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">which is exactly the Bellman optimality equation for <math id="A1.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q^{\ast}_{\mathcal{M}^{\prime}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q^{\ast}_{\mathcal{M}^{\prime}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
By uniqueness of the fixed point, <math id="A1.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{Q}(s,a)=Q^{\ast}_{\mathcal{M}^{\prime}}(s,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Q}(s,a)=Q^{\ast}_{\mathcal{M}^{\prime}}(s,a)</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e.,</span></p>
<table id="A1.E44" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E44.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q^{\ast}_{\mathcal{M}^{\prime}}(s,a)=Q^{\ast}_{\mathcal{M}}(s,a)-\eta\Phi(s)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q^{\ast}_{\mathcal{M}^{\prime}}(s,a)=Q^{\ast}_{\mathcal{M}}(s,a)-\eta\Phi(s).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(44)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS4.p2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS4.p2.3.1" class="ltx_text">Since the shift term <math id="A1.SS4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-\eta\Phi(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\eta\Phi(s)</annotation></semantics></math> does not depend on <math id="A1.SS4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>, the maximizing action is unchanged for every <math id="A1.SS4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>,
so <math id="A1.SS4.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> preserves the optimal policy of <math id="A1.SS4.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Extended Preliminaries</h2>

<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Intrinsic exploration</h3>

<div id="A2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Exploration is a key bottleneck in sparse-reward tasks, where extrinsic feedback provides little guidance for discovering reward-relevant trajectories. A common approach augments the environment reward with an intrinsic bonus, i.e.,
<math id="A2.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{\prime}_{t}=r_{t}+\eta\,r_{t}^{\mathrm{int}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>int</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{\prime}_{t}=r_{t}+\eta\,r_{t}^{\mathrm{int}}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> controls the contribution of intrinsic motivation. Prior work designs <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{t}^{\mathrm{int}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>int</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{t}^{\mathrm{int}}</annotation></semantics></math> from novelty signals, such as information gain, pseudo-count measures, or prediction error in forward models and disagreement among ensembles. While effective in some domains, especially in low-dimensional domains, these can be dominated by task-irrelevant visual factors, leading to inefficient exploration.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>Backbone framework</h3>

<div id="A2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In MetaWorld experiments, our method and most of visual RL baselines are implemented on top of the off-policy DrQ-v2 framework, which has become a widely adopted backbone for pixel-based continuous-control benchmarks. Given an encoder <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{\omega}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>ω</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{\omega}</annotation></semantics></math>, DrQ-v2 trains a double-Q critic <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{\vartheta_{k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Q</mi><msub><mi>ϑ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{\vartheta_{k}}</annotation></semantics></math> using an <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>-step bootstrapped TD loss:</p>
<table id="A2.E45" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E45.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{Q}(\vartheta_{k},\phi_{\omega})=\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{D}}\!\left[Q_{\vartheta_{k}}(\phi_{\omega}(s_{t}),a_{t})-\Big(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\gamma^{i}r_{t+i}+\gamma^{n}\min_{k=0,1}Q^{\mathrm{tgt}}_{\bar{\vartheta}_{k}}(\phi_{\omega}(s_{t+n}),a_{t+n})\Big)\right]^{2}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>Q</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ϑ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>ω</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><msub><mi>ϑ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>ω</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><munderover><mo lspace="0em" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munderover><mrow><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>n</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><munder><mi>min</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ϑ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><mi>tgt</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>ω</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{Q}(\vartheta_{k},\phi_{\omega})=\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{D}}\!\left[Q_{\vartheta_{k}}(\phi_{\omega}(s_{t}),a_{t})-\Big(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\gamma^{i}r_{t+i}+\gamma^{n}\min_{k=0,1}Q^{\mathrm{tgt}}_{\bar{\vartheta}_{k}}(\phi_{\omega}(s_{t+n}),a_{t+n})\Big)\right]^{2},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(45)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q^{\mathrm{tgt}}_{\bar{\vartheta}_{k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ϑ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><mi>tgt</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q^{\mathrm{tgt}}_{\bar{\vartheta}_{k}}</annotation></semantics></math> is a slowly-updated target critic (EMA). The actor <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\nu}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ν</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\nu}</annotation></semantics></math> is optimized to maximize the critic value,</p>
<table id="A2.E46" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E46.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\pi}(\nu)=-\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{D}}\!\left[\min_{k=0,1}Q_{\vartheta_{k}}\big(\phi_{\omega}(s_{t}),\,\pi_{\nu}(\phi_{\omega}(s_{t}))+\epsilon(t)\big)\right]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>π</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><munder><mi>min</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><msub><mi>ϑ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>ω</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ν</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>ω</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\pi}(\nu)=-\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{D}}\!\left[\min_{k=0,1}Q_{\vartheta_{k}}\big(\phi_{\omega}(s_{t}),\,\pi_{\nu}(\phi_{\omega}(s_{t}))+\epsilon(t)\big)\right],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(46)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">with exploration noise <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon(t)\sim\mathrm{clip}(\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{t}^{2}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>clip</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon(t)\sim\mathrm{clip}(\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{t}^{2}))</annotation></semantics></math>. DrQ-v2 further improves sample efficiency by applying lightweight image augmentations, while typically updating <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{\omega}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>ω</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{\omega}</annotation></semantics></math> only through the critic.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Experimental Details</h2>

<section id="A3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.1 </span>MetaWorld Tasks</h3>

<figure id="A3.F6" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18724v1/figures/mw_vis.png" id="A3.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/131;" width="476" height="131" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A3.F6.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 6</span>: </span><span id="A3.F6.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Example vision tasks in the MetaWorld environment.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In Figure <a href="#A3.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ C.1 MetaWorld Tasks ‣ Appendix C Experimental Details ‣ Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, we show four representative manipulation tasks from the Meta-World benchmark <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yu et al., 2020</a>)</cite>: <span id="A3.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Box-close</span>, <span id="A3.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Stick-pull</span>, <span id="A3.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Pick-out-of-hole</span>, and <span id="A3.SS1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Coffee-push</span>. These tasks share a common structure in requiring precise, multi-stage object interactions, while differing in contact patterns and control objectives.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="A3.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A3.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A3.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Box-close</span> requires the agent to grasp or push a box lid and rotate it until the box is fully closed, demanding accurate spatial alignment and force application.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A3.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A3.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Stick-pull</span> involves grasping a stick and pulling an object toward a target region, emphasizing directional control through tool-mediated interaction.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A3.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A3.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Pick-out-of-hole</span> focuses on extracting an object from a cavity, which requires coordinated grasping and vertical lifting under tight spatial constraints.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A3.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A3.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Coffee-push</span> asks the agent to push a mug to a designated goal position, relying on sustained contact and long-horizon pushing behavior.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Due to the use of high-dimensional pixel-based observations, intrinsic reward mechanisms like prediction error or novelty estimation can become unreliable. Agents may be misled by minor visual fluctuations—such as lighting changes, texture noise, or background shifts, which artificially inflate intrinsic reward signals. As a result, intrinsic motivation methods (e.g., RND or ICM) may overestimate the novelty of visually altered yet semantically identical states. This sensitivity to visual distractions degrades the stability of exploration and hinders efficient policy learning in sparse reward environments.</p>
</div>
</section>

</table>
</span></div>
</figure>
<div id="A3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A3.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ C.2 MetaWorld Experiments ‣ Appendix C Experimental Details ‣ Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> reports the best episode success rates, in MetaWorld tasks. In general, TEB achieves the highest performance in most of tasks, indicating that the proposed metric-based exploration not only accelerates learning, but also achieves a stronger final performance. The gains are most pronounced on harder manipulation tasks where sparse feedback and long-horizon coordination matter: on <span id="A3.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Pick-out-of-hole</span>, TEB reaches <math id="A3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="93.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>93.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">93.1\%</annotation></semantics></math>, outperforming the strongest baseline ICM (<math id="A3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="76.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>76.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">76.1\%</annotation></semantics></math>) while CeSD and CTRL-SR fail to solve the task; on <span id="A3.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Push-back</span>, TEB attains <math id="A3.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="98.4\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>98.4</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">98.4\%</annotation></semantics></math>, exceeding RAP (<math id="A3.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="65.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>65.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">65.0\%</annotation></semantics></math>) and DrM (<math id="A3.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="61.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>61.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">61.1\%</annotation></semantics></math>) by a large margin. TEB also remains consistently strong on <span id="A3.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Stick-pull</span> and <span id="A3.SS2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Coffee-push</span>. The only exception is <span id="A3.SS2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Box-close</span>, where ICM slightly leads (<math id="A3.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="97.3\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>97.3</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">97.3\%</annotation></semantics></math> vs. <math id="A3.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96.8\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>96.8</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96.8\%</annotation></semantics></math>), suggesting that when the task provides relatively easier success feedback, generic curiosity can match peak returns. Notably, the small standard deviations of TEB across all tasks indicate stable convergence.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.3 </span>Maze2D Experiments</h3>

<figure id="A3.F7" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18724v1/figures/maze_fig.jpg" id="A3.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/286;" width="476" height="286" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A3.F7.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 7</span>: </span><span id="A3.F7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Comparison of the learning curves of TEB and baselines in Maze environments with 100k training steps. Each experiment runs with 10 random seeds, with shaded region representing the standard deviation across seeds.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.4 </span>Learning Curves in Maze2D</h3>

<div id="A3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in Figure <a href="#A3.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ C.3 Maze2D Experiments ‣ Appendix C Experimental Details ‣ Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>, we also present the learning curves among TEB and the exploration baselines over 100K training steps. We can see that TEB (blue line) significantly outperforms all baselines in both learning speed and maximum exploration coverage across Maze2D tasks, especially in <span id="A3.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Square_a</span> and <span id="A3.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Square_a</span>. Furthermore, we observe that most baselines, such as LBS and RND, converge early and cease generating valuable transitions, while also achieving low exploration capabilities. CeSD, a promising method, does not converge in most tasks, remaining in stable exploration, but its efficiency is relatively low. Overall, the curve comparisons strongly demonstrate that the exploration bonus based on the predictive bisimulation metric yields the best exploration abilities.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">

</div>
<div id="alg1.l20" class="ltx_listingline">
              
              
               Update target critics: <math id="alg1.l20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q^{\text{tgt}}\leftarrow\tau Q+(1-\tau)Q^{\text{tgt}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>Q</mi><mtext>tgt</mtext></msup><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Q</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>Q</mi><mtext>tgt</mtext></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q^{\text{tgt}}\leftarrow\tau Q+(1-\tau)Q^{\text{tgt}}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="alg1.l20.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l21" class="ltx_listingline">
              
              
              <span id="alg1.l21.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">end</span> <span id="alg1.l21.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">for</span>
</div>
<div id="alg1.l22" class="ltx_listingline">
              
              
             <span id="alg1.l22.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">end</span> <span id="alg1.l22.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">for</span>

<section id="A3.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.6 </span>Baselines Details in Maze2D Experiments</h3>

<div id="A3.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We summarize the background of all exploration and skill discovery baselines used in Maze2D experiments.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS6.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ICM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Pathak et al., 2017</a>)</cite></span> proposes a curiosity-driven exploration mechanism where an intrinsic reward is defined by the prediction error of a forward dynamics model. This method encourages agents to explore transitions that are hard to predict, reflecting novel experiences.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS6.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS6.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">RND <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Burda et al., 2018</a>)</cite></span> utilizes a fixed random target network and a trained predictor. The prediction error serves as an intrinsic reward signal, helping agents detect novel states in a scalable and robust manner.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS6.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS6.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Disagreement <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Pathak et al., 2019</a>)</cite></span> estimates explorations based on the disagreement among an ensemble of forward models. High disagreement across the ensemble indicates uncertainty, promoting exploration of under-sampled areas.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS6.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS6.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ProtoRL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yarats et al., 2021b</a>)</cite></span> integrates prototype representations into RL, encouraging exploration toward underrepresented clusters in the state space. This structured exploration improves sample efficiency and diversity of learned behaviors.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS6.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS6.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LBS <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mazzaglia et al., 2022</a>)</cite></span> applies Bayesian surprise not in parameter space but in a learned latent space of dynamics. This approach is more computationally efficient and more robust to stochastic environments.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS6.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS6.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">DIAYN <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Eysenbach et al., 2018</a>)</cite></span> learns diverse skills in the absence of reward by maximizing mutual information (MI) between skills and the resulting states. Each skill should generate distinguishable behavior trajectories .</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS6.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS6.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">SMM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee et al., 2019</a>)</cite></span> aims to flatten the state visitation distribution by minimizing KL divergence between the current state distribution and a target. This entropy-based method improves exploratory coverage.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS6.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS6.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LSD <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Park et al., 2022</a>)</cite></span> imposes Lipschitz constraints on skill learning objectives to enforce local continuity. This helps prevent mode collapse and ensures skills generalize across similar states.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS6.p10.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS6.p10.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">BeCL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2023</a>)</cite></span> proposes a contrastive learning objective for skill discovery by treating skill-conditioned trajectories as different views. It maximizes MI between behaviors under the same skill, promoting both diversity and consistency.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.p11" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS6.p11.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS6.p11.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">CeSD <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bai et al., 2024</a>)</cite></span> develops an approach where multiple skills explore distinct clusters of state space. It introduces distributional constraints to ensure that skills visit non-overlapping regions, thereby improving coverage and distinguishability.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Method Details</h2>

<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>Pseudo-code Algorithm</h3>

<div id="A4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We describe the TEB algorithm in Algorithm <a href="#alg1" title="Algorithm 1 ‣ C.5 Exploration Visualizations in Maze2D ‣ Appendix C Experimental Details ‣ Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.2 </span>Hyperparameter settings</h3>

<div id="A4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in Table <a href="#A3.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ C.5 Exploration Visualizations in Maze2D ‣ Appendix C Experimental Details ‣ Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, we provide shared training hyperparameters in MetaWorld and Maze2D. In the Maze experiments, we calculated the state coverage obtained by each algorithm by discretizing the map for each task into tiny bins. Specifically, we set the discrete cell size to 0.1 for <span id="A4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Square_bottleneck</span> and <span id="A4.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Square_tree</span>, and 0.05 for the others. Additionally, details of TEB-specific hyperparameters are provided below. First, the coefficient <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{R}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{R}=1</annotation></semantics></math> is used for the reward differential term, the coefficient <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{T}=\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{T}=\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> within the predictive Bisimulation metric. The variance bounds <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{min}=1e-4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{min}=1e-4</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{max}=1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{max}=1.0</annotation></semantics></math> are used to train the Gaussian predictor of the reward. The loss weight for Gaussian predictor training of reward is <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{r}=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{r}=0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, the dynamics model is <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{p}=1e-4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{p}=1e-4</annotation></semantics></math>, and bisimulation metric is <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{b}=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{b}=0.5</annotation></semantics></math>. Finally, we set the intrinsic reward weight <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta=1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta=1.0</annotation></semantics></math> for most MetaWorld, except for <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta=0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta=0.05</annotation></semantics></math> for <span id="A4.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Stick-pull</span> and <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta=10</annotation></semantics></math> for <span id="A4.SS2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Push-back</span>. Since the extrinsic reward has been normalized, we set <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math> by initial intrinsic reward below 0.05, so the choice of <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math> is not complicated.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><cite class="ltx_cite"><span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_citation ltx_ref_self">langley00</span></cite></p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
